reviews.quote: 16GB of memory isn't a lot when it needs to be shared (and even when I just had a lot of browser tabs open, 11GB would already be in use).

professional.notes: No outlet reviewed the 64GB tier (added to the line after launch). Ratings inferred from CNET 8.3 anchor with RAM uplift; see SHARED-surface-pro.md.

praises: 64GB makes the Pro 11 a genuine mobile workstation for VMs, large datasets, and local LLMs in a 895 g tablet
OLED 120Hz screen + silent fanless chassis combination remains unmatched at any price
Battery unaffected by the RAM — still ~a full workday (family trait verified by CNET)
Replaceable M.2 2230 SSD under kickstand even on the flagship
Deep-sale pricing (reg $4,999 → $3,679.98 at BBY) makes the max tier surprisingly reasonable
complaints: Reg CA$5,400 with keyboard is laptop-ultra money for ARM Windows app caveats
CPU/GPU identical to the $1,849 tier — you pay purely for RAM
DX12 gaming and GPU compute still Adreno-limited; big RAM doesn't fix drivers
No headphone jack, 2 ports, glossy reflections — same line-wide gripes
Virtually no user reviews at CA retail (0 at BBY) — thin real-world track record for this tier

design_philosophy: The halo configuration Microsoft added post-launch to prove the Copilot+ platform's ceiling: 64GB of memory for on-device AI and pro multitasking in the same fanless 895 g OLED tablet. It embodies the line's tiering logic — identical X Elite silicon at every rung, with memory as the paid upgrade axis.
rating_notes: Inferred from CNET 8.3 anchor on 16GB/1TB OLED (SHARED-surface-pro.md): +48GB RAM → productivity +1.2, ai_ml +1.3 (64GB enables multi-billion-param local models), creative_work +0.7; battery −0.1 (marginally more memory power draw). Fanless X Elite throttles under sustained all-core load, capping productivity despite RAM.
